messages:
michael: Heads-up — canary pool A (nf4/qa tag) started showing a sustained throughput drop ~20% since the NF4/FP4 calibration change rolled at 09:12 UTC. Also seeing a memory jump ~3.8GB on a subset of hosts. link: https://perf.redwood/example-run
anya: Confirming. Spike aligns with the calibration commit (sha: b7f3a2c). Canary traffic stats: successful qps down, p95 latency up ~40ms.
samir: Any kernel fallback logs? Could be selector choosing slow int4 kernels for long seqs.
michael: Checked kernel selection trace — for seq_len=512 we see repeated hits to the slow path (kernel v3-fallback) instead of v3-fast. Trace snippet: `kernel_selector: chosen=v3-fallback reason=heuristic_mismatch batch=8 seq=512`
jyoti: That's odd — batching heuristics were supposed to prefer fast kernels for mid-size batches. Did calibration change alter model ops that influence kernel scoring?
michael: Perf dump attached (small excerpt):
```
profile: sample 1: seq=512 batch=8 kernel=v3-fast time=18.2ms
profile: sample 2: seq=512 batch=8 kernel=v3-fallback time=34.7ms
profile: sample 3: seq=128 batch=32 kernel=v3-fast time=9.1ms
mem: before=12.1G after=15.9G host=gpu-17
```
anya: hot path looks double latency when fallback chosen. Also seeing KV cache churn metrics: slab_evictions++ and kv_lookup_miss rate increased by ~2.5x around the same time.
samir: Could calibration have increased KV prefill size (more keys) causing allocator fragmentation? What does allocator telemetry show?
michael: allocator summary: free_chunks=low, slab_util=87%, avg_fragment_size=48kb. We previously saw ~72% util.
jyoti: That would explain memory spike. If slab_util went up due to larger per-request KV footprints, eviction could trigger and then more host->device memcpy, slowing kernels.
perf-bot: auto-bisect started for canary group A against last good commit (sha: a335c0f). Tests queued: kernel-selection, batching-heuristics, kv-allocator.
anya: Quick repro plan: rollback calibration on 2 canaries, repro load with seq=512, batch=8 synthetic trace. If throughput recovers -> calibration is top suspect.
michael: I ran offline microbench: toggling quant-calib flag `use_combined_stats=false` drops fallback selection dramatically and restores throughput to ~97% baseline. Command: `./bench --model my-nf4 --seq 512 --batch 8 --calib-flag false`
samir: Interesting. That flag changes how per-tensor scale stats are aggregated; could shift op ranges and hit different codepaths in quant kernels.
jyoti: For immediate mitigation can we force kernel selector override for seq>=256 to prefer v3-fast? Add an escape hatch in routing policy until calibration is fixed. Any side-effects?
michael: We tried forced selector in staging: no correctness regressions in smoke; perf improved, mem pressure slightly lower. But it's a temporary knob — still want root cause.
anya: Next steps: 1) revert canary -> reduce customer impact. 2) run full bisect on calibration commit to find which stat change caused kernel score delta. 3) add selector telemetry (emit chosen_score delta) and sampling heatmap for seq/batch combos. 4) investigate allocator behavior under new calib (replay traces).
samir: I'll own bisect (start time 09:40 UTC). Jyoti can you run allocator replay and mem-sim on the calibration diffs? Michael can prepare selector telemetry PR.
jyoti: On it — will run mem-replay and a fragmentation sweep (tool: alloc-replay --trace canary-A --calib b7f3a2c). Expect results in ~45m.
perf-bot: bisect update: preliminary suspect range narrowed to commits b7f3a2c..b7f3b80 (changes to quant scale accumulation).
michael: Uploading a small patch that makes selector emit `score_fast - score_fallback` as metric and samples it every 30s. PR: https://git.redwood/r/sel-telemetry
anya: Good. If bisect confirms it's scale aggregation we need to either adapt kernel scoring or add a small calibration postprocess to clamp outliers. Could also tweak batching heuristic to favor combos that keep fast kernels.
samir: Agree. Also add an E2E regression test that runs a handful of seq/batch combos through calibration and ensures kernel selector doesn't flip to fallback for our common paths.
jyoti: alloc-replay finished: mem spike reproduced; fragmentation rises after ~1200 requests under the new calib. Saving profile at https://perf.redwood/memdump/2941239876.
michael: Ok let's start rollback on canary group A now. I'll kick deploy rollback at 09:52 UTC. Keep monitoring metrics for p95 and slab_evictions.
anya: Thanks — keep updates here. We'll collate findings into a short postmortem and add mitigations to rollout checklist (telemetry, rollback plan, e2e kernel-selector test). :thumbsup:
